How to assess AI fluency in minutes
TestGorilla makes it easy to create a perfectly tailored assessment for your role that answers the all-important question: is this candidate AI-fluent? Here's how it works.
Create your first job
Give us a few details about your company and the role, including how AI shows up in the day-to-day. We then recommend the tests and interview questions that match the kind of AI fluency your role needs.
Make resumes earn their place
When applications arrive, our Resume Scoring tool reads each one against your job description and ranks it on fit. With Explainable Scoring, you see exactly why each candidate scored the way they did — and you can always override it, so you're fully in control.
Confirm the candidate, not just their claims
Our ID Verification tool confirms a candidate is who they say they are in under 30 seconds, with a government ID and a live selfie. It's privacy-first and stores no ID data, so honest candidates breeze through before the assessment starts.
Use qualifying questions
Use qualifying questions to screen out anyone who misses a hard requirement early. You only focus on those who are role-relevant.
Don't ask them about AI. Ask them to use AI
Assess if they're truly AI-fluent. Filter our test library by AI fluency and you get every test and interview tied to our five pillars of AI fluency in one place.
Measure real capability
Go beyond multiple-choice theory with scenario-based tasks. Candidates show you how they choose a tool, verify an output, and know when to step back from AI entirely.
Go deeper before interviews are required
Use our AI Interviews feature to measure a candidate against all five pillars in one sitting, adapted to your role. These interviews are run by an AI avatar and feel like a real call.
Every assessment is benchmarked
Every assessment is benchmarked against expert ratings, not just AI output. Every score is explainable. No black box, no arbitrary number — just a breakdown you can defend in the debrief.

AI fluency is the ability to use AI tools effectively, critically, and responsibly at work. That means knowing when to apply AI, how to prompt it, how to verify its output, and where its limits are. At TestGorilla, we measure it across five behaviors: applied use, learning agility, systems thinking, responsible use, and one more — together forming a framework built for the realities of modern work.
AI literacy is understanding what AI is and how it works. AI fluency is the applied skill of using AI well to get reliable results in real work. A fluent person knows when AI helps and when it doesn't, catches its mistakes, and moves faster with fewer rework loops.
Literacy is knowing the rules of the road. Fluency is driving in traffic.
With practical, scenario-based tasks rather than multiple-choice questions about AI. Candidates do realistic work using AI, and our scoring captures not just the output but how they got there: which tool they chose, what they verified, and when they decided not to use AI at all.
Every score is benchmarked against expert ratings and explained, so you can see exactly why a candidate scored the way they did.
As AI tools become standard at work, AI fluency predicts how productively a new hire can actually use them. The cost of getting it wrong is real: 59% of organizations that defined AI fluency still made a bad AI hire — someone who interviewed well and couldn't execute.
Assessing fluency directly is how you avoid hiring confidence instead of competence.
No. AI fluency matters across marketing, product, operations, HR, customer success, and more. The behaviors are the same across functions even when the tools differ.
Our framework is built to travel across roles, not just screen engineers. You can build an AI fluency assessment for any role on your org chart.
